newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian-Russian Corporate Bank raises capital.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian-Russian Corporate Bank raises capital.

text.p: The joint Bulgarian-Russian Corporate Commercial Bank decided on Thursday to raise capital to 2.2 billion levs from 800 million levs through a rights issue, the bank's chief executive director said.
"The shareholders meeting voted today for a capital rise to 2.2 billion levs to meet central bank minimum capital requirements," Ventsislav Antonov told Reuters.
Under Bulgarian National Bank's (BNB) requirements local commercial banks should have a minimum capital of 2.2 billion for a full licence and 1.4 billion levs for a domestic one by March 31, 1997.
Corporate bank's share capital is 61 percent held by Bulgaria's state-owned Bulbank (Bulgarian Foreign Trade Bank) and the remaining 39 percent by Russia'a Vnesheconombank.
The Corporate Bank was set up in 1994 as a successor to the Bulgarian-Russian Bulsovinvest financial company.
